objects_built.name: purge_old_support_tickets
objects_built.role: Daily deletes support_tickets rows with created_at older than 730 days (retention cleanup for retained tag)

objects_changed.name: delete_user_account
objects_changed.change: Added db.bulk.delete support_tickets where user_id == input.user_id; added tags = ["erasure"]

templates_considered: retained_data_has_age_limit (RET-003): fit, used for the 730-day retention rule

recipe 'Erase and expire personal data' (GDPR): fit as the basis; its build used erase_user_data, a new endpoint, and sensitive field attributes, which I left out because DELETE /account and delete_user_account already exist and the ask does not cover field classification
CONF-011 / DATA-010 / LOG-001: in the GDPR recipe, not used; the ask does not mention field classification, response content or logs
RET-002 (retained data has a cleanup task): not used; RET-003 already requires a task with a max-age cutoff

rules.covers: When a user deletes their account, every personal table is deleted from by the erasure function
Customer data is not kept longer than 2 years (support tickets only)

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Orders, payments, invoices, refunds keep user references after account deletion
2-year limit on user accounts and customers (inactivity clock, which date counts)
Completeness of erasure (right rows, user notified)
Copies at AI summariser, mail/payment vendors, backups, logs, other tenants/branches

assumptions: Support tickets belong to the user when user_id is set; tickets with only requester_email are not linked and are not deleted on erasure
2-year retention is measured from created_at for support_tickets
Financial records (orders, payments, invoices, refunds) are out of scope for deletion pending the owner's decision
Tag placement: tags = [...] line after auth = false / auth = true in table files, and after response in function files (accepted by dry-run)
confusions: Skill recipe for GDPR erasure assumes no erasure endpoint exists; here DELETE /account and delete_user_account already exist, so the recipe's build list does not apply directly
Warnings for tags that the plan itself creates ('is on no table on this branch') are expected but the skill says never accept a warning; no guidance on warnings for tags added in the same change
Skill does not show how to set tags on functions or tasks in XanoScript; I inferred tags = [...] placement from the workspace's workflow_test and endpoint files
No guidance on how to write guid for new objects; I left guid out of the new task file and dry-run accepted it
wished_for: A short example of tags placement for table, function and task XanoScript files
Guidance on whether a retention rule should count from created_at, last_login_at, or both, for user-linked data
A recipe variant for an account that already has an erasure endpoint
why_confidence: The policy checks that a personal-tagged table is deleted from by a tagged function and that support tickets have a 730-day cleanup task. It does not cover orders, payments or the inactive-user 2-year limit, and it cannot see whether erasure is complete or what vendors keep. Dry run passed, but evaluate has not been run, so findings are unknown.
